requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, except for the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.ci.span` has no structural obligations, and it has no implementation roots, which fits that. Each clause states observable parsing behavior:

- **Opening fence.** The clause is "an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`". A parser built with a regex, a hand-written scanner or a Markdown library would accept the same inputs and give the same results.
- **Closing fence.** The clause is "at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace". It describes which inputs close a block. It does not say how to build the parser.
- **Indentation.** The clauses are "indented by up to three spaces" and "four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence". These are input-acceptance rules.
- **Body.** The clauses are "all Markdown between those fence lines ... except for the header option lines" and "MUST NOT include text after the closing fence". These are output-content rules.
- **Whitespace.** The clause is "Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing". It describes comparison behavior.

The text names no required library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface. Any implementation that produces the same spans would satisfy it, so how the parser is built is discretionary. The cited `requirements.references.anchors` is only context. It supplies the option-line exclusion, and its own obligations are judged against its own text. Tests supply the evidence for the behavior.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each observable obligation in `requirements.ci.span`, and their assertions enforce the expected outcomes.

**Opening fence**
- It needs at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`.
- `closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent` asserts that `::{req}`, `::: {req}` and `:::{req}ready` are not definitions.
- Fences of 3, 4 and 7 colons are accepted in `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` and `validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers`.

**Closing fence**
- It needs at least as many colons as the opener, with nothing else on its line except whitespace.
- `validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers` closes `::::` with `::::` and `:::::`, and closes `:::::::` with `::::::::`.
- `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` shows that a nested `:::` does not close a `::::` block, and it checks the exact body span.
- `closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent` shows that `:::foo` does not close, while `::: ` with trailing whitespace does.
- `reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence` checks the unclosed case and its error message.

**Indentation**
- A fence may be indented by up to three spaces, and a line indented four or more spaces is not a fence.
- The same test asserts that a three-space-indented opener and closer work.
- It also asserts that a four-space opener yields no definition and that a four-space closer leaves the block unclosed.

**Body content**
- The body is all Markdown between the fences, including headings, examples, diagrams and blank lines.
- `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` includes a code block with a heading and a `:::` line, a following ATX heading, and a setext heading. Evidence matching the full body validates.
- `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` covers blank lines and a code block containing `{req}`.
- The `:::` line inside the code block does not close the body in that test. The text does not state that case, so I treated this as the intended reading and not a gap.

**Option lines**
- Header option lines of `requirements.references.anchors` are excluded from the body.
- `anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text` checks `without_options` and the rendered output, and checks that non-leading `:impl:` and `:test:` text stays in the body.
- `anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable` shows that evidence with the option lines omitted gives no "text changed" error.

**No text after the closing fence**
- The following-text exclusion is checked for a colon-fenced requirement in `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text`. Its evidence matches only the exact body.
- It is also checked for longer closers in `validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers` and by the `blocks[0].end` assertion in `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive`.

**Whitespace**
- Leading and trailing whitespace is excluded when comparing with evidence.
- `requirement_bodies_are_compared_without_surrounding_whitespace` uses indented text with trailing spaces and blank lines, and evidence holding the trimmed text validates.

No obligation is left untested, and all the relevant tests carry `{test}` markers for this requirement.

text: :::{req} span

A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, except for the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
